title: Choose the appropriate visa type for your situation
description: Portugal offers D7 (passive income), D8 (digital nomad), Golden Visa, and other options. Research which fits your situation best.

title: Confirm your consulate jurisdiction
description: Portuguese visa applications are usually tied to where you legally reside. Confirm the correct consulate before preparing documents.

title: Decide on a target city or region
description: Lisbon, Porto, Algarve, and Madeira are popular choices. Consider cost of living, weather, and community.

title: Create a relocation budget
description: Factor in visa fees, flights, initial housing, health insurance, and 3-6 months of living expenses.

title: Gather proof of income or savings
description: D7 requires proof of passive income (pension, investments, rental). D8 requires proof of remote work income.

title: Obtain criminal background check
description: Get an FBI background check (for US citizens) and have it apostilled. Some consulates require it translated to Portuguese.

title: Get birth/marriage certificates apostilled
description: Obtain certified copies and apostilles from the issuing state. Translation may be required.

title: Secure health insurance valid in Portugal
description: Travel insurance is needed for the visa application. You'll switch to Portuguese health insurance (SNS or private) after arrival.

title: Write a cover letter / statement of purpose
description: Explain why you want to move to Portugal, your plans, and how you'll support yourself.

title: Schedule visa appointment at consulate
description: Book early - appointments can be limited. Bring all required documents in the specified format.

title: Submit visa application
description: Attend your appointment with all documents. Pay the visa fee. Processing takes 2-4 months typically.

title: Book temporary accommodation for first weeks
description: Airbnb or short-term rental for 2-4 weeks while you search for permanent housing and complete initial bureaucracy.

title: Schedule SEF/AIMA appointment for residence permit
description: After arriving, you need to schedule an appointment with immigration (SEF/AIMA) to get your residence card.

title: Get NIF (tax identification number)
description: Required for almost everything - banking, housing, utilities. Can be obtained at Finanças or through a fiscal representative.

title: Open Portuguese bank account
description: Major banks include Millennium BCP, Novo Banco, Santander. You'll need NIF and proof of address.

title: Register with local health center
description: Register at your local Centro de Saúde to access the Portuguese public health system (SNS).

title: Find long-term housing
description: Search on Idealista, Imovirtual, or Facebook groups. Be prepared for competitive market in Lisbon/Porto.

title: Set up utilities
description: Electricity (EDP), water, gas, internet. Some landlords include utilities in rent.

title: Get Portuguese phone number
description: Major carriers: MEO, NOS, Vodafone. Prepaid SIMs are easy to get; contracts require NIF.

title: Attend SEF/AIMA appointment for residence card
description: Bring all required documents. You'll receive your residence card (Título de Residência) after approval.
